candidates.source_name: CBCG — Platni sistem (payment system hub: RTGS + DNS)
candidates.why_relevant: Central Bank of Montenegro is owner AND operator of the national payment system (RTGS gross real-time + DNS deferred net). This hub page defines system components, participation model (direct participation only), technical standards (ISO 20022 MX, SWIFT BIC, IBAN, IP/MPLS VPN extranet) and links to RTGS/DNS sub-pages, tariffs and statistics. It is the canonical anchor for the whole cell.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Recurring HTML crawl of the hub plus its sub-pages (/rtgs-sistem, /dns-sistem, /pregled-tarife-centralne-banke-crne-gore, /statistika-platnog-prometa); diff for standard/participation changes. Both /me/ and /en/ (and /r/) locale prefixes exist.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on operator/system terms, then direct fetch and sub-link snowball

CBCG "pravila rada" platni sistem RTS/X DNS učesnici odluka

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Pravila rada Platnog sistema Centralne banke Crne Gore (payment system rulebook PDF)
candidates.why_relevant: The actual participant rulebook: RTGS operating procedures, participant-to-system communication, suspension/exclusion powers of the central bank, cut-off and settlement mechanics. This is the single highest-value document for participant obligations and rule changes; versions of it are what banks must implement against.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic PDF download with hash/version diffing; also watch the parent 'propisi/pl_promet' directory pattern for sibling rulebooks and amendments.

negative_findings.description: No national payment-QR standard for Montenegro was found. Searching 'QR kod plaćanje standard' in Serbian/Montenegrin returned Serbia's NBS IPS QR ecosystem and Montenegro's fiscal-invoice QR requirement, but no CBCG-issued payment QR specification, generator or validator.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language QR queries surfaced only fiscalisation QR (tax invoices) for Montenegro; the payment-initiation QR hits were all Serbian (ips.nbs.rs) or unrelated (QRIS, QR Ph).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A national QR overlay is a normal follow-on to an instant-payment go-live and would carry merchant/PSP technical deadlines. Its apparent absence is itself intelligence: either it does not yet exist, or it lives inside not-yet-public instant-payment scheme documentation.

negative_findings.description: No domestic card switch / national card scheme operator was identified for Montenegro — no equivalent of a DinaCard, BKM or national ATM-sharing network with its own rulebook and participant circulars.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches for a Montenegrin card switch returned only international schemes (Visa/Mastercard), bank lists, and third-party processors (ChipCard/ASEE, Ingenico POS at NLB Montenegro). No designated domestic scheme body surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If no national card scheme exists, card-side rule changes for Montenegro originate from Visa/Mastercard global releases plus CBCG regulation, which changes where the collection effort should point. This needs confirmation, not assumption.

negative_findings.description: I had no confirmed Montenegrin-language brand or acronym for a domestic card scheme or switch to search with, so the card-scheme leg of this cell was searched mainly with English and generic Serbian terms.
negative_findings.result_summary: Queries used generic terms ('kartično procesiranje', 'card scheme', vendor names). Without a real local brand name, recall is likely incomplete.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Local-language coverage for the card-scheme sub-topic is weaker than for instant payments and RTGS/DNS; a missed local brand would mean a missed rulebook publisher.

brief: Montenegro's payments infrastructure is unusually centralised: CBCG is owner, operator, rule-maker and overseer of the national payment system (RTGS + DNS, relaunched as the ISO 20022-native RTS/X in May 2025) and also of the instant-payment system built on Banca d'Italia's TIPS software, live since 20 July 2026 under a Western Balkans TIPS-clone arrangement announced by the ECB. That means nearly all binding participant material — the Pravila rada rulebook PDF, the odluke index under CBCG's podzakonski akti, tariffs, oversight and statistics — sits on cbcg.me, with the primary-law layer and its public consultations on gov.me and the legal effective dates in Službeni list Crne Gore. The externally verifiable participant view comes from the European Payments Council registers and rulebooks, since Montenegro entered SEPA geographical scope in November 2024 with an operational readiness date of 5 October 2025 and CBCG holds an EPC licence for the scheme rules. The clear white space in this cell is the card and QR layer: no domestic card scheme or switch and no national payment-QR standard surfaced (only fiscal-invoice QR and Serbia's NBS IPS QR as a comparator), so card-side intelligence currently depends on processor and vendor disclosures such as ChipCard/ASEE rather than on any national scheme body.
